title: 2. Retirement of Partners
subtitle: New Ratio, Gaining Ratio, Revaluation, Goodwill, Settlement of Dues, Admission cum Retirement

questions.q: Retirement of a partner results in:
options: Reconstitution of the partnership firm
Winding up of the business
Compulsory dissolution of the firm
Insolvency of the firm

questions.q: Gaining ratio is calculated as:
options: New ratio minus old ratio
New ratio plus old ratio
Old ratio minus new ratio
Old ratio divided by new ratio

questions.q: The concept of gaining ratio is specifically used to determine compensation payable by:
options: The new partner to the old partners
Partners whose share of profit increases, to the partner(s) whose share decreases
The firm to outside creditors
Partners whose share decreases, to partners whose share increases

questions.q: On retirement, if no new ratio is specified, continuing partners are presumed to share future profits:
options: In the capital ratio
In their old mutual ratio
Equally, regardless of the old ratio
In the gaining ratio divided by two

questions.q: At retirement, assets and liabilities are revalued through a:
options: Memorandum Capital Account
Profit and Loss Appropriation Account only
Revaluation Account
Realisation Account

questions.q: Profit or loss on revaluation at retirement is shared by:
options: All partners, including the retiring partner, in the old profit-sharing ratio
All partners equally, irrespective of the old ratio
Only the continuing partners, in the new ratio
Only the retiring partner

questions.q: On retirement, the retiring partner's share of goodwill is compensated by the continuing partners in their:
options: Capital ratio
Old profit-sharing ratio
New profit-sharing ratio before retirement
Gaining ratio

questions.q: If goodwill already appears in the firm's books at retirement, it is usually written off among all partners (including the retiring partner) in their:
options: Gaining ratio
Old profit-sharing ratio
New profit-sharing ratio
Capital ratio

questions.q: On retirement, the balance in the retiring partner's Capital Account, after all adjustments, represents:
options: The continuing partners' combined capital
The amount due to the retiring partner
The gaining ratio
The firm's total capital

questions.q: As per Section 37 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, if the amount due to a retiring partner is left in the business, the retiring partner (or representative) is entitled, at their option, to:
options: Immediate dissolution of the firm
No compensation whatsoever
Interest at 6% per annum on the amount due, or such share of profits as is attributable to the use of that amount
A fixed penalty of 10% per annum

questions.q: The amount due to a retiring partner may be settled by:
options: Converting it into the continuing partners' capital without consent
Lump sum payment, instalments with interest, or transfer to a loan account
Compulsory transfer to the Reserve Fund only
Writing it off as a bad debt

questions.q: When the amount due to a retiring partner is not paid immediately, it is commonly transferred to a:
options: Suspense Account
Retiring Partner's Loan Account
Drawings Account
Realisation Account

questions.q: If a retiring partner's dues are settled in instalments, interest is usually calculated:
options: On the outstanding balance, at the agreed rate
Only if the partner demands it in writing every year
Only on the original total amount, regardless of repayments
Never, since instalment payments do not attract interest

questions.q: "Admission cum retirement" refers to a situation where:
options: Two partners retire simultaneously
A new partner is admitted and an existing partner retires at or around the same time
A partner is admitted without any change in the profit-sharing ratio
The firm is dissolved and reconstituted as a company

questions.q: In an admission-cum-retirement scenario, the new profit-sharing ratio must account for:
options: Both the incoming partner's share and the effect of the outgoing partner's retirement
Only the outgoing partner's share
Only the incoming partner's share
Neither; the old ratio continues unchanged

questions.q: On retirement, reserves and accumulated profits appearing in the Balance Sheet are distributed among:
options: All partners, including the retiring partner, in the old profit-sharing ratio
Only the retiring partner
Only the continuing partners
Nobody; they are carried forward unchanged

questions.q: An increase in the value of an asset at the time of retirement is:
options: Debited to the Goodwill Account
Debited to the Revaluation Account
Credited to the retiring partner's Capital Account directly
Credited to the Revaluation Account

questions.q: A provision found to be in excess at the time of retirement is:
options: Transferred directly to the Realisation Account
Credited to the Revaluation Account
Ignored, since provisions are never revalued
Debited to the Revaluation Account

questions.q: On retirement, if continuing partners adjust their capitals to the new profit-sharing ratio, a partner with capital in excess of the required amount:
options: Withdraws the excess, or transfers it to a loan/current account
Has the excess transferred to the retiring partner automatically
Has the excess written off as a loss
Must bring in additional capital instead

questions.q: If the retiring partner's Capital Account shows a debit balance after all adjustments (the partner owes the firm), this amount is:
options: Recovered from the retiring partner
Automatically written off as a loss to the firm
Transferred to the Goodwill Account
Ignored, since retiring partners can never owe the firm

questions.q: On retirement, unrecorded assets discovered are:
options: Ignored
Credited to the Revaluation Account
Credited to the retiring partner's account only
Debited to the Revaluation Account

questions.q: On retirement, unrecorded liabilities discovered are:
options: Debited to the Revaluation Account
Ignored
Debited to the retiring partner's account only
Credited to the Revaluation Account

questions.q: The retiring partner's share of profit up to the date of retirement, where retirement occurs during an accounting year, is usually calculated on the basis of:
options: The firm's total assets at the date of retirement
The entire year's profit, regardless of the date of retirement
The continuing partners' combined capital
Time elapsed, or sales/turnover since the last Balance Sheet, as agreed

questions.q: Interest on a retiring partner's loan account, where applicable, is generally:
options: Charged as an expense in the firm's Profit and Loss Account
Ignored in the firm's accounts
Treated as a reduction in the continuing partners' capital only
Credited directly to the Revaluation Account

questions.q: A partnership firm continues to exist even after a partner retires, provided:
options: At least five partners remain
The remaining partner obtains government approval
The firm is immediately registered as a company
A minimum of two partners remain

questions.q: On retirement, the Capital Accounts of continuing partners are affected by:
options: The retiring partner's personal expenses only
Nothing; only the retiring partner's account is affected
The firm's sales revenue only
Their share of revaluation profit/loss, goodwill adjustment, and reserves

questions.q: If the retiring partner is paid partly in cash and partly through a loan account, the cash portion is recorded as a:
options: Debit to the retiring partner's Capital Account and credit to Bank/Cash
Credit to the Goodwill Account
Credit to the retiring partner's Capital Account and debit to Bank/Cash
Debit to the Revaluation Account

questions.q: The primary purpose of calculating a new profit-sharing ratio on retirement is to:
options: Determine how continuing partners will share future profits and losses
Calculate the income tax payable by the firm
Value the firm's goodwill only
Determine the retiring partner's final dues only

questions.q: Where partners' capitals are fixed, adjustments relating to revaluation and goodwill on retirement are passed through:
options: The partners' Capital Accounts
The Drawings Account
The partners' Current Accounts
The Realisation Account

questions.q: Goodwill of the firm, for retirement purposes, is generally valued using the same methods as used at the time of:
options: Preparation of the firm's income tax return
Admission of a partner
Insolvency of a partner
Dissolution of the firm

questions.q: When goodwill is not raised in the books at retirement, the continuing partners' Capital Accounts are debited, in their gaining ratio, and the retiring partner's account is:
options: Left unaffected
Credited with the firm's total goodwill
Debited with their share of goodwill
Credited with their share of goodwill

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a valid method of settling the amount due to a retiring partner?
options: Automatic transfer to the firm's Reserve Fund without the partner's consent
Transfer to a Loan Account
Payment in a lump sum
Payment in instalments with interest

questions.q: A retiring partner remains liable to third parties for the firm's acts:
options: For an unlimited period after retirement, regardless of any agreement
Only if the retiring partner was the managing partner
Never, once retirement is effective
Done before retirement, unless discharged by agreement with the third party

questions.q: Public notice of retirement is important primarily because:
options: It limits the retiring partner's liability for the firm's future acts to third parties
It is required to calculate the new profit-sharing ratio
It is required only for admission, not retirement
It determines the gaining ratio

questions.q: If the Revaluation Account at retirement shows a loss, it is:
options: Ignored in the final settlement
Debited only to the retiring partner's Capital Account
Credited to all partners' Capital Accounts in the old ratio
Debited to all partners' Capital Accounts in the old ratio

questions.q: The final amount payable to a retiring partner typically includes:
options: Only the firm's total assets divided by the number of partners
Capital balance, share of reserves, share of revaluation profit, and share of goodwill, less drawings or amounts owed
Only the share of goodwill
Only the original capital contributed

questions.q: When continuing partners adjust capitals after retirement and a partner's capital falls short of the required amount, that partner:
options: Automatically retires as well
Brings in additional capital to make up the shortfall
Receives a compulsory loan from the retiring partner
Has the shortfall written off as a firm loss

questions.q: Retirement of a partner differs from dissolution of the firm in that retirement:
options: Automatically converts the firm into a company
Always results in the closure of the business
Allows the firm to continue in existence with the remaining partners
Requires a court order in every case

questions.q: On retirement, if the gaining partners also owe the retiring partner a share of accumulated reserves, this is adjusted:
options: Along with the goodwill and revaluation adjustments, in the retiring partner's final settlement
Only if the firm is dissolved subsequently
Separately, a full year after retirement
Through the firm's Profit and Loss Appropriation Account of the following year only

questions.q: The core accounting objective on retirement is to ascertain:
options: The exact amount due to the outgoing partner and fairly restate the continuing partners' capitals
The firm's total annual turnover
The market value of the firm's brand name
The personal income tax liability of the retiring partner
